## Summary

- Catalog object Relations now provides inline relation authoring, relation summaries and actions, and explicit-target path lookup in one workspace.
- A relation graph view makes connected objects and their joins easier to inspect alongside the relation list.
- Human and Metadata MCP callers can create joins across Sources. Explicit-target join-path lookup can traverse connected cross-Source graphs when the caller can read both endpoints.
- Catalog embedding readiness is published behind the shared embedding fence, preventing stale runs from marking a newer embedding configuration ready.
- Channel canvas arrangement discards stale results after graph adoption, unmount, locking, or geometry and measurement changes, rather than applying an obsolete layout.

## Operator notes

- Upgrade from v0.9.0 using the standard replace-and-start procedure. This release adds no schema revision, required environment variable, or manual data migration.
- Download this release's `docker-compose.yaml` and `prometheus.yml` and replace both site files. Keep the live `.env`; the environment example is attached as `default.env.example`. No environment keys changed in this release.
- Run `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`. Keep the existing PostgreSQL volume and mount at `/var/lib/postgresql`. Never run `docker compose down -v` unless site data should be destroyed. Sites still using only the v0.1.8 deployment must complete the volume move described in the v0.1.10 notes before upgrading.
- The minor version bump reflects a Site HTTP API and Metadata MCP semantic change: cross-Source join creation and explicit-target path lookup no longer return `JOIN_CROSS_SOURCE` solely because the endpoints belong to different Sources. Batch join creation no longer requires every pair to share one Source. Callers that branch on that error must update their assumptions.
- Source access checks still apply. Open-ended path exploration and question-ranked (`q` / `query_text`) lookup remain inside the start Source graph; only explicit-target lookup traverses connected cross-Source graphs. Rejected joins remain excluded from path traversal.
- Entity MCP and Webhook delivery contracts are unchanged. Existing catalog records, channel versions, and run snapshots are not rewritten by this release.
